# Taxes and exemptions (TAX)

How each line is taxed: VAT rates, reverse charge, exempt and non-subject operations, OSS, disbursements, IRPF and the currency amounts are expressed in.

Rules page: https://docs.beel.es/rules/taxes

"Checked by: Your integration" or "The issuing business" means BeeL. does not enforce the rule, beyond any error codes it lists: the integration has to.

## TAX-001

**Apply the VAT rate in force when the operation took place**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. rejects the cases listed under the error codes; the rest is yours to check.

Each taxed line carries the VAT rate that applied on the date the operation accrued, not the one in force on the day you issue. The rate must also be one AEAT accepts for a subject, non-exempt line.

**Why:** A rate that was not in force at accrual charges the wrong tax, and AEAT checks the rate against the operation date: the record is rejected or the invoice has to be corrected.

**Applies to:** operations `createCompanyInvoice`, `patchCompanyInvoice`, `createCompanyCorrectiveInvoice`; Lines taxed with IVA (main_tax.type: IVA).

**Error codes:** [`INVALID_VAT`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/INVALID_VAT)

**Legal basis:**

- Ley 37/1992 del IVA, art. 90.Dos — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1992-28740#a90
- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.1 TipoImpositivo — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** Invoicing in October a supply that accrued in June at the rate that applies in October, because it is the one in force on the issue date.

**Correct:** Sending operation_date with the June date and the rate that applied in June on each line.

```json
{ "operation_date": "2026-06-18", "lines": [{ "description": "Supply", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 100, "main_tax": { "type": "IVA", "percentage": 21 } }] }
```

**Related:** DAT-004, TAX-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/tax-classification#allowed-main_taxpercentage-values

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-001.md

## TAX-002

**Reverse-charge operations are invoiced without charging VAT**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

When the recipient is the one liable for the VAT, as in the cases of art. 84.Uno.2.º LIVA, the line does not charge VAT: classify it as reverse charge with the exemption_reason of its case. Deciding that an operation falls under reverse charge is the issuer's call.

**Why:** Charging VAT on a reverse-charge operation makes both parties declare it: the issuer collects a tax it does not owe and the recipient self-assesses it again.

**Applies to:** invoice types `STANDARD`, `CORRECTIVE`; Operations where the recipient is the taxpayer (inversión del sujeto pasivo).

**Legal basis:**

- Ley 37/1992 del IVA, art. 84.Uno.2.º a) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1992-28740#a84
- Ley 37/1992 del IVA, art. 84.Uno.2.º f) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1992-28740#a84

**Incorrect:** A contractor invoicing construction work to the developer charges 21 % VAT on the line.

**Correct:** The line goes at 0 % with the reverse-charge reason of its case.

```json
{ "description": "Construction work, phase 2", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 25000, "main_tax": { "type": "IVA", "percentage": 0 }, "exemption_reason": "ISP_ART_84_2_F" }
```

**Related:** TAX-003, CNT-012, CNT-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/tax-classification#inversión-del-sujeto-pasivo-s2

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-002.md

## TAX-003

**Reverse-charge lines carry no tax and never go on a simplified invoice**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. rejects a request that breaks it.

A reverse-charge line goes at 0 % with no tax amount, and only on a full invoice or its correctives, never on a simplified one. It cannot carry an equivalence surcharge nor use the OSS regime.

**Why:** AEAT registers a reverse-charge line only with rate and tax amount at zero, and only on invoice types that identify the recipient, who is the one who self-assesses.

**Applies to:** invoice types `STANDARD`, `SIMPLIFIED`, `CORRECTIVE`; Lines classified as reverse charge (exemption_reason ISP_ART_84_2_*).

**Error codes:** [`LINE_EXEMPTION_WITH_TAX`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/LINE_EXEMPTION_WITH_TAX), [`SIMPLIFICADA_FORBIDS_ISP`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/SIMPLIFICADA_FORBIDS_ISP), [`ISP_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_SURCHARGE`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/ISP_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_SURCHARGE), [`OSS_REGIME_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_ISP`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/OSS_REGIME_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_ISP)

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.4 CalificacionOperacion — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** A simplified invoice with a reverse-charge line: the API answers SIMPLIFICADA_FORBIDS_ISP.

**Correct:** A standard invoice to the identified business recipient, with the line at 0 % and its reverse-charge reason.

**Related:** TAX-002, SIM-003, SUR-001

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/tax-classification#rules-beel-enforces

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-003.md

## TAX-004

**Intra-EU supplies of goods are exempt only with the buyer's EU VAT number**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. rejects the cases listed under the error codes; the rest is yours to check.

An intra-EU supply of goods is exempt only when the buyer has a VAT number from another Member State and has given it to you, and the recipient goes on the invoice with that number as an alternative identifier of type NIF-IVA. The operation must also be declared in the recapitulative statement (modelo 349), outside BeeL.

**Why:** Without a valid EU VAT number the exemption does not apply and Spanish VAT was due; AEAT also rejects an E5 record that does not identify the recipient that way.

**Applies to:** invoice types `STANDARD`, `CORRECTIVE`; Goods shipped to a business in another EU Member State (exemption_reason: EXENTA_ART_25).

**Error codes:** [`EXEMPTION_REQUIRES_RECIPIENT_ID_TYPE`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/EXEMPTION_REQUIRES_RECIPIENT_ID_TYPE)

**Legal basis:**

- Ley 37/1992 del IVA, art. 25.Uno — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1992-28740#a25
- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.5.1 OperacionExenta E5 — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** Invoicing goods to a French company as exempt with the recipient identified only by name: the API answers EXEMPTION_REQUIRES_RECIPIENT_ID_TYPE.

**Correct:** Identifying the customer with its EU VAT number as alternative_id of type NIF-IVA, after checking that the number is valid.

**Related:** CNT-005, CNT-021, TAX-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/international-customers#b2b-intra-eu--goods-e5

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-004.md

## TAX-005

**Exempt and non-subject lines carry no VAT rate**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. rejects a request that breaks it.

A line with an exemption_reason goes at 0 %: it carries neither a VAT rate nor a tax amount, and no equivalence surcharge.

**Why:** AEAT does not accept a rate or a tax amount on an exempt or non-subject line; the invoice would say the operation is exempt and charge VAT at the same time.

**Applies to:** Lines with an exemption_reason (exempt, non-subject or reverse charge).

**Error codes:** [`LINE_EXEMPTION_WITH_TAX`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/LINE_EXEMPTION_WITH_TAX)

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.4 y 3.1.3.15.5 — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** A training course marked EXENTA_ART_20 sent at 21 %: the API answers LINE_EXEMPTION_WITH_TAX.

**Correct:** The same line at 0 % with its exemption reason.

```json
{ "description": "Vocational training course", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 400, "main_tax": { "type": "IVA", "percentage": 0 }, "exemption_reason": "EXENTA_ART_20" }
```

**Related:** CNT-010, TAX-003

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/tax-classification#rules-beel-enforces

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-005.md

## TAX-006

**Services to a business abroad are not subject to Spanish VAT**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: medium · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

A service to a business established in another country is, as a general rule, located where the customer is established: invoice it without Spanish VAT, as not subject by location rules (NO_SUJETA_LOCALIZACION), and identify the customer. The exceptions of art. 70 LIVA (real estate, events, transport and others) need their own analysis.

**Why:** Charging Spanish VAT on a service located abroad collects a tax Spain is not owed, and the customer cannot deduct it.

**Applies to:** invoice types `STANDARD`, `CORRECTIVE`; Services to a business customer established outside Spain, general rule.

**Legal basis:**

- Ley 37/1992 del IVA, art. 69.Uno.1.º — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1992-28740#a69

**Incorrect:** A software consultancy invoices a German company at 21 % Spanish VAT.

**Correct:** The line goes at 0 % with exemption_reason: NO_SUJETA_LOCALIZACION and the customer is identified with its EU VAT number.

**Related:** TAX-004, TAX-007, CNT-021

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/international-customers#b2b-intra-eu--services-n2 · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/international-customers#services-to-non-eu-customers

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-006.md

## TAX-007

**Sales declared through OSS use regime key 17**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. rejects the cases listed under the error codes; the rest is yours to check.

An operation you declare through the OSS or IOSS one-stop shop goes with regime key 17, classified as not subject by location rules. Whether your sales are above the OSS threshold of 10,000 € a year, and so under OSS, is yours to decide.

**Why:** AEAT identifies one-stop-shop sales by the regime key; under another key the record says Spanish VAT was charged on a sale taxed in another country.

**Applies to:** Distance sales and B2C services to other EU countries declared in the OSS or IOSS one-stop shop.

**Error codes:** [`REGIME_REQUIRES_INCOMPATIBLE_EXEMPTION`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/REGIME_REQUIRES_INCOMPATIBLE_EXEMPTION), [`OSS_REGIME_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_ISP`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/OSS_REGIME_INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_ISP)

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Preguntas frecuentes SIF y VERI*FACTU, Registros de facturación: alta (OSS) — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/iva/sistemas-informaticos-facturacion-verifactu/preguntas-frecuentes/registros-facturacion-alta.html

**Incorrect:** An online shop above the OSS threshold invoices a consumer in Italy at 21 % under the general regime 01.

**Correct:** The line goes with regime key 17, the Italian VAT rate and exemption_reason: NO_SUJETA_LOCALIZACION.

**Related:** TAX-006, TAX-003

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/regime-keys#17--oss--ioss · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/international-customers#b2c-intra-eu--above-the-oss-threshold

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-007.md

## TAX-008

**Disbursements go as suplido lines, without tax**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. rejects a request that breaks it.

An amount you paid in the customer's name and on their behalf is not part of your taxable base: send it as a SUPLIDO line, which carries no VAT, surcharge or IRPF.

**Why:** Taxing a disbursement charges VAT on money that was never your income; AEAT only accepts it in the total as a non-subject or zero-rated amount.

**Applies to:** Amounts paid on behalf of the customer (suplidos).

**Error codes:** [`LINE_SUPLIDO_MUST_HAVE_NO_TAX`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/LINE_SUPLIDO_MUST_HAVE_NO_TAX)

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Preguntas frecuentes SIF y VERI*FACTU, Registros de facturación: alta (suplidos) — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/iva/sistemas-informaticos-facturacion-verifactu/preguntas-frecuentes/registros-facturacion-alta.html

**Incorrect:** A gestoría adds the registry fee it paid for the client as a normal line at 21 %.

**Correct:** The fee goes as a suplido line.

```json
{ "line_type": "SUPLIDO", "description": "Registry fee paid on your behalf", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 35.20 }
```

**Related:** TAX-009

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/suplidos

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-008.md

## TAX-009

**IRPF withholding is not part of the total AEAT receives**

`MUST NOT` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

The IRPF withheld on an invoice is not part of its billing record: the total AEAT receives is the total before the withholding, so it can differ from the amount payable. BeeL. leaves the withholding out of the record for you.

**Why:** Comparing the QR amount or the registered total with the amount payable and reading the difference as an error leads to correcting an invoice that is right.

**Applies to:** Invoices with IRPF withholding, under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Preguntas frecuentes SIF y VERI*FACTU, Registros de facturación: alta (retenciones) — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/iva/sistemas-informaticos-facturacion-verifactu/preguntas-frecuentes/registros-facturacion-alta.html

**Incorrect:** Flagging as a mismatch an invoice whose QR says 121.00 while the customer pays 106.00 after a 15 % withholding.

**Correct:** Reconciling payments against the amount payable, and the AEAT record against the total before withholding.

**Related:** TAX-010, TAX-008

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/what-aeat-receives#the-total · https://docs.beel.es/guides/amounts-and-rounding#irpf

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-009.md

## TAX-010

**Set the IRPF withholding when the customer must withhold**

`SHOULD` · BeeL. rule · Impact: medium · Checked by: Your integration. BeeL. rejects the cases listed under the error codes; the rest is yours to check.

When your customer has to withhold IRPF from your invoice, set irpf_rate on each line, one of 0, 1, 2, 7, 15, 19 or 24. BeeL. shows the withholding and takes it off the amount payable; a simplified invoice never carries it.

**Why:** Without the withholding on the invoice the customer pays the full amount, and one of you ends up correcting it with the tax authority.

**Applies to:** invoice types `STANDARD`, `CORRECTIVE`; Professionals invoicing a business or professional that has to withhold IRPF.

**Error codes:** [`INVALID_IRPF`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/INVALID_IRPF), [`SIMPLIFICADA_FORBIDS_IRPF`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/SIMPLIFICADA_FORBIDS_IRPF)

**Incorrect:** A freelance consultant invoices a company without irpf_rate, and the company has to ask for a corrected invoice.

**Correct:** The line carries the withholding.

```json
{ "description": "Consulting, September", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 1000, "main_tax": { "type": "IVA", "percentage": 21 }, "irpf_rate": 15 }
```

**Related:** TAX-009, SIM-003

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/amounts-and-rounding#irpf

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-010.md

## TAX-011

**Cash-basis lines stay domestic, subject and not reverse charge**

`MUST NOT` · AEAT criterion · Impact: low · Checked by: AEAT. AEAT rejects a record that breaks it.

A line under the cash-basis regime (07) cannot be reverse charge nor non-subject, and cannot use the exemptions of articles 21 to 25 LIVA (exports and intra-EU supplies).

**Why:** AEAT rejects the record, and with BeeL. that happens after the invoice has been issued and numbered, so fixing it takes a corrective or a void.

**Applies to:** Lines under the cash-basis regime (regime key 07).

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.6.5 ClaveRegimen 07 — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** A cash-basis business puts an intra-EU supply of goods (EXENTA_ART_25) under regime key 07.

**Correct:** Only domestic, subject operations go under 07; the intra-EU supply goes under its own regime and exemption.

**Related:** CNT-013, TAX-004

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/regime-keys#07--cash-basis-iva-criterio-de-caja

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-011.md

## TAX-012

**The tax and the billing record are expressed in euros**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: medium · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

An invoice may state its amounts in another currency, but the VAT charged is expressed in euros, and every amount in the billing record is in euros. BeeL. invoices only in euros, so both hold for every invoice it issues.

**Why:** AEAT only takes tax and record amounts in euros; a foreign-currency amount would have to be converted at the exchange rate the law sets.

**Applies to:** Every invoice.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1619/2012 (Reglamento de facturación), art. 12.1 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2012-14696#a12
- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 10.2 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a10

**Incorrect:** Expecting BeeL. to register a dollar invoice and convert it for AEAT.

**Correct:** Converting the price to euros before sending it, as TAX-013 says.

**Related:** TAX-013

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/amounts-and-rounding#precision

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-012.md

## TAX-013

**Send every amount in euros**

`MUST` · BeeL. rule · Impact: critical · Checked by: Your integration. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

The API has no currency field: every amount you send is read as euros. Convert foreign-currency prices to euros before sending them; you may mention the original currency in the notes.

**Why:** A price sent in dollars or pounds is invoiced, taxed and registered with AEAT as that many euros, and only a corrective fixes it.

**Applies to:** operations `createCompanyInvoice`, `patchCompanyInvoice`, `createCompanyCorrectiveInvoice`

**Incorrect:** Passing through a Stripe charge of 100 USD as unit_price: 100.

**Correct:** Converting it first and sending the euro amount, with the original amount in notes.

```json
{ "notes": "Original charge: 100.00 USD", "lines": [{ "description": "Subscription, September", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 92.40 }] }
```

**Related:** TAX-012

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/amounts-and-rounding#precision

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/TAX-013.md
